gloss: to go to pick someone up; to go to meet someone

definitions.gloss: to go to pick someone up; to go to meet and bring someone back
definitions.explanation: To travel to a location in order to meet someone and accompany or transport them back. Commonly used for picking up children, guests, or family members.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもを{迎|むか}えに{行|い}く。
examples.english: I'm going to pick up my child.

examples.japanese: {空港|くうこう}まで{友人|ゆうじん}を{迎|むか}えに{行|い}った。
examples.english: I went to the airport to pick up my friend.

examples.japanese: {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}ってきたから、{駅|えき}まで{傘|かさ}を{持|も}って{迎|むか}えに{行|い}こうか。
examples.english: It started raining, so shall I go to the station with an umbrella to pick you up?

notes:
A very common everyday expression using the pattern verb stem + に{行|い}く (to go in order to do something). The verb {迎|むか}える means to welcome or receive, and combined with に{行|い}く it specifically means going somewhere to meet and bring someone back.

USAGE:
- {迎|むか}えに{行|い}く means you go to the other person's location
- {迎|むか}えに{来|く}る means someone comes to your location to pick you up
- Often used with を to specify who you're picking up: {子|こ}どもを{迎|むか}えに{行|い}く

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {子|こ}どもを{迎|むか}えに{行|い}く: to pick up one's child
- {空港|くうこう}に{迎|むか}えに{行|い}く: to go to the airport to pick someone up
- {駅|えき}まで{迎|むか}えに{行|い}く: to go to the station to meet someone
- {車|くるま}で{迎|むか}えに{行|い}く: to go pick someone up by car

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {迎|むか}えに{来|く}る: to come to pick someone up — the reverse perspective
- {送|おく}り{迎|むか}え: pickup and drop-off — the noun form covering both directions
